title: Place the workload only when location and authority agree
description: Select a workload contract, a platform footprint, and an administrative authority model. The decision evaluates data surfaces, control planes, operators, dependencies, and unilateral provider access separately.
modelNote: This teaching model illustrates control contracts. Accountable legal and risk owners must define the actual requirements for each workload and jurisdiction.

workloads.label: Public service catalog
workloads.detail: Published service descriptions with no resident records or restricted operational data.
workloads.legalBoundary: No mandatory localization in this model; integrity and continuity still require ownership and evidence.

workloads.label: Resident benefits records
workloads.detail: Identifiable applications, eligibility decisions, supporting documents, and administrator activity.
workloads.legalBoundary: All regulated copies stay in the home jurisdiction under customer-held identity and key authority.

workloads.label: Restricted investigation files
workloads.detail: Highly restricted records whose administration and recovery must continue without an external provider authority.
workloads.legalBoundary: Data, control, operations, and recovery remain inside the home authority with no critical external dependency.

platforms.label: Global managed SaaS
platforms.detail: The provider chooses several storage and operating locations behind one global service.
platforms.dependencyNote: Global identity, control plane, key service, support tooling, and service metadata.

platforms.label: Local public-cloud region
platforms.detail: Primary service data is pinned locally, while some control, support, and telemetry systems remain global.
platforms.dependencyNote: Global account identity, provider control plane, and support workflow.

platforms.label: Locally operated sovereign zone
platforms.detail: Data surfaces and daily operations are local, with a bounded signed-update dependency.
platforms.dependencyNote: A mirrored and verified provider software update channel.

platforms.label: Customer-operated private stack
platforms.detail: The customer runs data, control, update approval, and recovery infrastructure inside its boundary.
platforms.dependencyNote: No external service is required for steady-state administration or recovery.

authorityModels.label: Provider-administered
authorityModels.detail: Provider roots issue administrator identities, release keys, and authorize privileged operations.

authorityModels.label: Customer identity and keys
authorityModels.detail: The customer controls administrator identity and key authorization; provider operations retain an emergency bypass.

authorityModels.label: Local dual control
authorityModels.detail: Customer roots control identity and keys; screened local operators require customer approval for privileged actions.
